title: upsertToken swallows all write failures — callers cannot detect a token that was never persisted
reasoning: upsertToken pipes the SQL insert through Effect.catch(() => Effect.succeed(undefined)), and the interface declares Effect<void, never>. Any D1 failure (constraint violation, driver error, quota) is converted into a successful completion, so the HTTP layer and callers proceed as though the token was persisted when it was not; the write is silently lost with no error surface and no logging. This contradicts the project's own documented pattern in token.service.ts lines 34-44, which deliberately surfaces read errors so HTTP callers can return 500 instead of a misleading success/empty response. The never error channel may be an intentional design choice, but the concrete impact (silent loss of user-submitted token data) is real.
recommendation: Change the error channel to Effect<void, TokenWriteError> (or similar) and let the HTTP layer map it to 500, or at minimum log the failure via Effect.tapError before swallowing; update the TokenService interface accordingly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for either service; nothing asserts behavior on D1 write failure.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock SqlClient to fail on INSERT and assert upsertToken fails (or, if swallowing is retained, that an observable log/telemetry signal is emitted).
minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/services/token.service.ts upsertToken and the TokenService interface (line 53).
